title: Safe Inputs but Unsafe Output: Benchmarking Cross-modality Safety Alignment of Large Vision-Language Models

bias_targets.methodology: Evaluating model responses to cross-modal inputs (a safe image and safe text that semantically combine to create an unsafe context) to detect racism, slurs, and racially insensitive outputs via text generation and multiple-choice QA tasks.
Assessing models on cross-modal queries designed to trigger sexism, gender marketing stereotypes, and gender-based hobby stereotyping to measure the rate of safe and effective responses.
Testing models with cross-modal inputs to measure the occurrence of cultural stereotyping, caste-based prejudice, and the misrepresentation of cultural symbolism.
Evaluating model responses to cross-modal scenarios involving disadvantaged groups to detect unfair treatment, prejudice, or disparaging remarks against people with disabilities.
Using cross-modal inputs to test for unfair treatment or disparaging outputs regarding socioeconomically disadvantaged or marginalized groups, such as the homeless.
Prompting models with cross-modal queries involving religious beliefs, dietary restrictions, sensitive topics, and rituals to evaluate whether the output is disrespectful, insensitive, or offensive.
Assessing cross-modal queries related to employment discrimination to detect unfair or unequal treatment in the workplace based on age.
Evaluating cross-modal employment scenarios to detect discriminatory outputs or unequal treatment based on sexual orientation.
